howTo.subtitle: Fill the grid. Keep your score low.
howTo.goalBody: Fill all 9 boxes of the grid, each with a Pokémon that fits both its row and its column.
howTo.coreBody: You get {pp} guesses (PP), and a wrong guess uses one too. Each Pokémon can be used once.
howTo.scoringBody: Fill as many boxes as you can. Your rarity score adds up the share of players who picked each of your answers: rarer picks, lower score.

rules.both: Every box needs a Pokémon that fits both its row and its column. Each Pokémon can be used once.
rules.pp: You get {pp} guesses (PP), and a wrong guess uses one too. Correct answers lock in.
rules.score: Your rarity score starts at 900 (100 for every empty box). Each pick counts the share of players who chose it in that box, so rarer picks pull it down. Lower is better. Your share card colours each box: 🟪 under 1%, 🟦 under 10%, 🟩 under 25%, 🟨 25% or more.
rules.filled: Filled counts your boxes. Tap Rarity to see the day's board.
rules.info: Tap the i on any category to see exactly what counts. When the game ends you see every valid answer for every box, and why each miss didn't fit.
rules.master: Every grid is checked to be solvable. Some days a hand-made Master Puzzle replaces the Daily Puzzle.

modeList.daily: Daily Puzzle: one grid a day, the same for everyone. Under More: Easy and Expert dailies, the themed Weekly grid and the Archive of past dailies (these never move your streak).
modeList.unlimited: Unlimited: a board you build yourself. Pick the rules (unlimited PP, guaranteed solvable, one-answer boxes, a timer), a difficulty and the categories you want, then generate as many as you like.
modeList.ttt: Tic Tac Toe: two trainers share a grid and take turns claiming boxes. Three in a row wins; a wrong guess or a timeout passes the turn.

kindList.types: Fighting, Dual-type, Monotype (one matching type is enough)
kindList.regions: Kanto to Paldea, by where a Pokémon debuted (a regional form counts for the region it debuted in)
kindList.evolution: No evolution line, Stone or Item evolution, Not fully evolved (an evolution counts from either side: Pikachu and Raichu are both a Stone evolution)
kindList.moves: A few famous moves, such as Surf or Earthquake (Expert adds deeper learnsets)
kindList.abilities: Expert only: well-known and obscure abilities
kindList.other: Legendary, Mythical, Paradox, Ultra-Beast, First Partner, Fossil, Baby, Mega, GMax (Expert adds stat thresholds)

rules.forms: Forms are their own picks: regional forms (Alolan Raichu), Megas (Mega Charizard X and Y), Gigantamax forms and a few notable forms (Partner Pikachu, Primal Kyogre, Origin formes, Crowned Zacian).
rules.own: A form's types, stats and abilities are its own. Its evolution line, legendary status and moves are its species'.
rules.region: A regional form counts for the region it debuted in: Alolan Raichu is from Alola, Galarian Meowth from Galar, Paldean Wooper from Paldea, Hisuian Growlithe from Hisui. A Mega or Gigantamax form counts for its species' region.
rules.reuse: No reuse: a form and its species are the same Pokémon. Once you use Charizard, Mega Charizard X is taken too, and the other way round. (Stricter than PokeDoku, where forms can repeat.)
rules.species: A species counts for 'Has an Alolan form' (and its forms of other regions); a type category needs just one of the Pokémon's types to match.
rules.moves: Move categories use the species' learnset from the latest main game it is in (Scarlet & Violet for most); stat categories use base stats.
rules.evolution: Evolution methods count from either side of the step: Pikachu (evolves with a Thunder Stone) and Raichu (evolved with one) both fit 'Stone evolution'.
